newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to back closing Wall Street tax loopholes.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to back closing Wall Street tax loopholes.

text.p: President Clinton will propose closing some corporate tax loopholes that affect Wall Street in the budget he presents to Congress on Thursday, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday.
"You will see proposals that deal with those issues," Rubin told reporters before a speech to the American Association of Retired Persons.
Administration officials had said earlier Clinton intends to resurrect a number of revenue-raising proposals that he made in his first term but which were not passed by Congress.
Among the proposals are elimination of a tax-avoidance scheme called selling short against the box and measures that would discourage the issuance of 100-year corporate bonds.
Rubin voiced optimism about the chances for an agreement between the administration and Congress on a balanced budget, saying that a pact was "highly likely."
"I think we can do it, I think we should do it and I think it is very likely we will put in place balanced budget legislation," he said.
He said he planned to meet House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich from Ohio and House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer from Texas today to discuss the budget.
